study_identification.title: Cortical thickness and grey-matter volume anomaly detection in individual MRI scans: Comparison of two methods

study_characteristics.study_objective: To compare the performance of normative modeling (ScanOMetrics) using metrics derived from two brain morphometry software tools (DL+DiReCT and FreeSurfer) for detecting statistical anomalies in individual MRI scans, particularly focusing on detecting cortical thickness and grey matter volume anomalies in patients with Alzheimer's disease compared to healthy controls.

hc_n.answer: 1828 (after cleaning; initially 1927 non-converting subjects with CDR=0)

hc_age.answer: mean 69.0; sd 9.3; min 42.7; max 97.0 (before cleaning, N=1927)

quality_checking_detail.answer: LOOCV-based outlier detection: scans with >5% abnormal raw regional metrics (18 or more out of 358 metrics with p<0.01) were flagged as anomalous. Initially 99 scans (5.15%) were removed from 1927 HC scans due to low image quality (susceptibility artifacts from dental implants), patient motion (blurring/ringing artifacts), or potential pathology (enlarged CSF space, prominent lateral ventricles suggestive of atrophy despite CDR=0). After cleaning, 1828 HC scans remained with reduced anomaly detection rate to 1.48% (27 scans).

site_effect_handling_detail.answer: Covariates including sex, scanner (Siemens Magnetom Sonata and Avanto at 1.5T, Biograph mMR and Magnetom Trio at 3T), and scanning protocol were accounted for by selecting matched subgroups before computing statistics. Matching for scanning protocol was used to reduce variability in thickness estimation due to imaging parameters and corresponding differences in WM/GM contrast. Age-matched reference scans (within 10% of age) were used for outlier detection and variability estimation.

modeling_method.answer: Polynomial regression (low order polynomials with adaptive degree selection via nested F-tests); Uniform age subsampling with outlier removal

response_variable.answer: Cortical grey matter volume (GMV); Cortical thickness (CTh) mean; Cortical thickness standard deviation; Subcortical volumes (thalamus, caudate, putamen, pallidum, accumbens area, hippocampus, amygdala, ventral diencephalon); Midline structure volumes (brain stem, 3rd and 4th ventricles); All metrics based on Desikan-Killiany atlas (34 cortical regions per hemisphere, 8 subcortical structures per hemisphere). Total of 597 metrics (358 raw + 239 normalized for brain size)

predictor_variables.answer: Age; Sex (via matching); Scanner type (via matching); Scanning protocol (via matching)

predictor_effects.answer: Age: fixed effect (polynomial regression); Sex, scanner type, and scanning protocol: handled via matched subgroup selection rather than explicit modeling as covariates

nm_vldtn_handle_ns.reason: The study addresses several aspects of nuisance structure: (1) Age nonlinearity is handled through adaptive polynomial fitting with degrees ranging 0-11. (2) Heteroscedasticity is partially addressed by computing metric variability as combination of variance over age-matched subjects (within 10% of age) and measurement uncertainty from repeated scans. (3) Scanner/protocol effects are handled through matched subgroup selection. (4) Outlier detection uses IQR-based methods applied twice (raw metrics and residuals). However, the study reports that Shapiro-Wilk tests indicated non-normal residual distributions for the vast majority of metrics (85-90% after cleaning), suggesting imperfect handling of distributional assumptions. Sex is only handled via matching rather than explicit modeling. No explicit discussion of within-site correlation, batch effects beyond scanner matching, or spatial autocorrelation.
nm_vldtn_handle_ns.supporting_text: Metric variability at a given age was computed by a combination of metric variance over subjects within 10% of the age of interest, and measurement uncertainty derived from repeated scans in the reference dataset... Covariates other than age (i.e. sex, scanner and scanning protocol) were accounted for by selecting matched subgroups before computing statistics... Shapiro-Wilk tests indicated that almost all metrics had non-normally distributed fit residues, with only minor improvements due to the cleaning procedures (decrease from 91% to 85% for DL+DiReCT and from 90% to 84% for FreeSurfer regarding the 358 raw metrics, and from 93% to 90% for DL+DiReCT and 98% without change for FreeSurfer regarding the 240 brain size normalized metrics).
nm_vldtn_handle_ns.location: Lines 119-121 (normative modeling section); Lines 123 (evaluation section); Lines 259 (cleaning results)

nm_vldtn_same_domain_nonindep.reason: The study performed extensive leave-one-out cross-validation (LOOCV) on the healthy control dataset. Subject-wise LOOCV was conducted where normative polynomial models were built excluding a specific HC (all sessions and repeated scans) and testing all scans of the excluded subject against that model. This was done for all 1927 HC scans initially, and repeated after cleaning on 1828 scans. Results showed 1.30% anomalous detections for DL+DiReCT and 1.16% for FreeSurfer at q=0.01 threshold (slightly above expected 1%). After cleaning, rates were 1.06% and 1.00% respectively. Shapiro-Wilk tests were performed on fit residues for each of 597 metrics. This represents thorough same-domain non-independent validation.
nm_vldtn_same_domain_nonindep.supporting_text: The normative dataset was evaluated with a subject-wise leave-one-out cross-validation (LOOCV) study, building normative polynomial models under exclusion of a specific HC (all sessions and repeated scans) and testing all scans of the excluded subject against that model... We assessed specificity of our approach to regional anomaly detection by running a subject-specific leave-one-out cross-validation (LOOCV) on the whole HC dataset. When considering the full set of tests made (358 raw metrics times 1'927 scans, yielding 689'866 p-values), and using a significance threshold of q = 0.01, processing the HC dataset with DL+DiReCT resulted in 8'911 significant p-values (1.30%, which is slightly but significantly higher than the expected 1%, pbinom < 1e-16).
nm_vldtn_same_domain_nonindep.location: Lines 147-149 (Methods section 2.10); Lines 273 (Results section 3.8); Lines 259 (Results after cleaning)

nm_vldtn_same_domain_indep.reason: The study used 87 MRI scans from 41 'converter' subjects (who had mixture of CDR=0 and CDR≥0.5 scans) that were explicitly excluded from building the normative model. These subjects were used to investigate change trajectories longitudinally. This represents independent data from the same domain (OASIS3) that was held out from model training. However, the analysis focused on longitudinal trajectories and atrophy progression rather than systematic validation of model performance metrics (e.g., calibration, explained variance). The validation was qualitative (examining atrophy patterns) rather than quantitative performance evaluation.
nm_vldtn_same_domain_indep.supporting_text: Of the 2'014 HC scans, 87 are from 41 subjects that had a mixture of scans with CDR = 0 and CDR ≥ 0.5 ('converters' between normal cognition and suspicion or established impairment). Those scans were excluded from building our normative model, which was therefore based on 1'927 scans from 696 non-converting subjects... The 41 'converter' subjects were instead used to investigate the change trajectories between the first and follow-up scans longitudinally... We used the 87 MRI scans of the 41 subjects that were excluded from building the normative models (conversion from CDR = 0 to CDR ≥ 0.5) to investigate the change of thickness over time in more detail.
nm_vldtn_same_domain_indep.location: Lines 82-84 (Methods section 2.1); Lines 195 (Results section on converters)

nm_vldtn_diff_domain.reason: The study compared ScanOMetrics outputs to two other normative modeling tools: PCN toolkit (Rutherford et al., 2022) and BrainChart (Bethlehem et al., 2022). Z-scores from ScanOMetrics for left and right mean cortical thickness were compared to PCN toolkit scores, showing strong correlation. Signed log(p) values were compared to BrainChart centiles, showing strong non-linear correspondence (Spearman rank correlation coefficient=0.950, p<1e-105). However, these comparisons used the same OASIS3 data rather than truly independent external datasets from different domains. The comparison validates consistency across methods but not generalization to different populations/scanners/protocols beyond what was in OASIS3.
nm_vldtn_diff_domain.supporting_text: Z-scores obtained when evaluating right and left mean CTh were compared to scores obtained using the PCN toolkit (Rutherford et al., 2022). Signed log(p) values for the average CTh were also compared to centiles obtained from Brain Chart (Bethlehem et al., 2022), another open-access tool for normative modelling. CTh for the HCs were submitted along the AD subjects for both PCN toolkit and BrainChart... Comparison of ScanOMetrics signed log(p) values (x-axis) and BrainChart's centiles (y-axis), showing a strong and non-linear correspondance between scores (Spearman rank correlation coefficient=0.950, p<1e-105).
nm_vldtn_diff_domain.location: Lines 135 (Methods section 2.7); Supplementary Figure S7 caption

deviation_metric.answer: Signed log10(p-value) where p-value is computed from z-score accounting for matched reference distribution and measurement uncertainty; Threshold for statistical anomaly: q=0.01 (equivalent to |log10(P)|>2); Percentage of abnormal metrics per scan (>5% = 18 or more of 358 raw metrics with p<0.01 considered anomalous scan); Normalized L2-distance between significance maps for comparing spatial patterns; ROC curve analysis using percentage of abnormal metrics

clinical_application_and_analysis.association_analysis: Group comparisons: Cohen's d effect size maps comparing AD vs HC groups. ROC analysis: AUC for scan classification (AD vs HC) based on percentage of abnormal metrics - DL+DiReCT AUC=0.76, FreeSurfer AUC=0.72. Region-specific ROC: entorhinal cortex thickness and hippocampal volume both achieved AUC=0.75. Stratification by CDR: percentage anomaly maps grouped by CDR levels (0.5, 1, ≥2) showing progression. Normalized L2-distance analysis: correlation between DL+DiReCT and FreeSurfer (r=0.87, p<1e-16); comparison across CDR levels showing negative association with disease severity. Scan-rescan reproducibility: L2-distance between repeated scans, Wilcoxon rank sum and signed rank tests. Longitudinal analysis: atrophy rates calculated for converter subjects; hippocampal atrophy rate ~6% annually for individual patient using DL+DiReCT, ~3% using FreeSurfer.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_findings_brief: Both DL+DiReCT and FreeSurfer normative modeling detected cortical thickness anomalies primarily in known AD predilection areas (bilateral entorhinal, fusiform cortex, precuneus, supramarginal gyrus), with AD scans showing up to twenty-fold more frequent anomalies than healthy controls, and DL+DiReCT processing >15 times faster (<25 min vs ~6 hours).
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_findings_detailed: Main findings: (1) Anomaly detection rates - 56-62% of AD scans (CDR≥1) were classified as anomalous (>5% abnormal metrics) compared to only ~1% of cleaned HC scans. (2) Regional specificity - Cortical thickness reductions detected in up to 28% of individual AD scans, with strong regional preference for bilateral entorhinal and fusiform cortex, precuneus, and supramarginal gyrus; frontal lobe showed weakest atrophy. (3) CDR progression - Using DL+DiReCT, abnormal entorhinal thickness detected in 24.8% of CDR=0.5, 47.2% of CDR=1, and 46.0% of CDR≥2 patients; using FreeSurfer: 17.6%, 30.2%, and 32.0% respectively. (4) Atrophy patterns matched group-level effects (Cohen's d maps) and published literature on AD. (5) Classification performance - ROC AUC=0.76 (DL+DiReCT) and 0.72 (FreeSurfer) for scan-level classification; region-specific AUC=0.75 for both tools using entorhinal thickness or hippocampal volume. (6) Longitudinal findings - In converter subjects, mean regional CTh reduced up to 0.1mm in temporo-basal regions (entorhinal, parahippocampal, fusiform, inferior temporal), equivalent to 25 years of normal aging; relative sparing of somatosensory cortex observed. Individual patient example showed ~6% annual hippocampal atrophy with DL+DiReCT. (7) Processing time - DL+DiReCT <25 min vs FreeSurfer >6 hours. (8) Reproducibility - Scan-rescan L2-distances significantly smaller for DL+DiReCT than FreeSurfer (p=9.2e-57 for AD, p=2e-309 for HC). (9) Residual variance - DL+DiReCT showed narrower distributions for thickness metrics (56 of 240 normalized metrics), while FreeSurfer showed narrower distributions for volume metrics (97 of 240). (10) Spatial correspondence between tools was high (r=0.87 for L2-distances, strong correlation with PCN toolkit and BrainChart).
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_limitations: Several limitations were identified: (1) Non-normal residual distributions - Shapiro-Wilk tests showed 85-90% of metrics had non-normally distributed fit residues even after cleaning, suggesting imperfect handling of distributional assumptions. (2) Scan classification accuracy modest - ROC AUC values ~0.72-0.76 indicate classification based on percentage of abnormal metrics or specific regional metrics is not sufficiently reliable for clinical diagnosis. (3) Heterogeneous individual patterns - Large variability in individual anomaly patterns despite shared group-level motifs, limiting diagnostic specificity. (4) Scanner/protocol effects - Only handled through matching rather than explicit harmonization modeling. (5) DL+DiReCT segmentation errors - Occasionally failed to capture full extent of regions, prone to failures with challenging WM/GM contrast. (6) FreeSurfer indexing errors - Occasional mislabeling of gyri (atlas-based identification errors). (7) Measurement uncertainty estimation - Based on rescans within 10% age change rather than same-session rescans, providing only upper bound of true uncertainty. (8) Limited to Desikan-Killiany atlas regions and subset of metrics jointly available from both tools. (9) Single dataset (OASIS3) limits generalizability. (10) No external validation on truly independent cohorts from different domains. (11) Clinical validation lacking - study is methodological comparison rather than clinical validation study. (12) Increased CTh in medial orbitofrontal gyrus may be artifact related to motion rather than true finding.
clinical_application_and_analysis.application_notes: Authors envision automated detection of statistical anomalies as trigger for secondary inspection by human expert (screening tool) rather than automated disease classification. They recommend DL+DiReCT for clinically-oriented morphometry when time and computing power are limiting factors, but recommend FreeSurfer when comparing to normative models developed with FreeSurfer for reproducibility. Future work should: (1) Combine normative modeling residues with AD classifiers and disease progression models. (2) Develop disease-specific quantitative reports (QReports) with GUI. (3) Conduct clinical evaluation studies comparing expert ratings with/without QReports. (4) Address heterogeneity of atrophy patterns across dementia subtypes. (5) Avoid data leakage in classifier development. Study provides complete reproducibility with open-source ScanOMetrics software, public OASIS3 dataset, online tutorials, and trained normative models made available to community.

general_notes.general_notes: This study is a methodological comparison paper comparing two processing pipelines (FreeSurfer vs DL+DiReCT) for normative modeling using the ScanOMetrics framework, applied to Alzheimer's disease detection. Key technical details: (1) Two scanners at different field strengths: 1.5T (Siemens Magnetom Sonata and Avanto, 42 scans) and 3T (Biograph mMR and Magnetom Trio, 2601 scans). (2) Brain size normalization: all volumes scaled to mean ICV of normative dataset; thickness scaled isometrically according to ICV^(1/3). (3) ICV estimates: eTIV for FreeSurfer, exhaustive volume sum for DL+DiReCT. (4) Uniform age subsampling: 100 resamples using 10-bin age histograms, drawing nmin (smallest bin count) samples from each bin. (5) Polynomial degree selection: nested F-tests with maximum degree = 2*floor(ln(n/10)+1)-1 (max degree 11 for n=1927). (6) Outlier removal: two-stage process using 1.5 IQR threshold applied to raw metrics then residuals. (7) Asymmetry indices computed for bilateral structures. (8) Total OASIS3 dataset: 2643 scans from 1038 participants; 2014 CDR=0, 420 CDR=0.5, 209 CDR≥1. (9) Hardware specs: Dell Precision 7920 with dual Intel Xeon Gold 6148 CPUs (20 cores each, 2.4GHz), 256GB RAM, NVIDIA GeForce GTX 1080 GPU (8GB), Ubuntu Linux 22.04.3 LTS. (10) Normative model fitting time: <10 min for 1828 HC scans. (11) Application to new case: <2 seconds. (12) 60 scans from 15 patients with CDR changing between different levels of CDR≥0.5 were excluded from demographic table for clarity. (13) ScanOMetrics code available at https://github.com/SCAN-NRAD/ScanOMetrics with documentation at https://scanometrics.readthedocs.io. (14) DL+DiReCT available at https://github.com/SCAN-NRAD/DL-DiReCT. (15) Funding: Swiss National Science Foundation (SNSF) Grants 204593 (ScanOMetrics) and CRSII5_180365 (Swiss-First Study). (16) Comparison tools: PCN toolkit and BrainChart showed strong correspondence with ScanOMetrics outputs. (17) Study emphasizes complete reproducibility with all tools open-source and dataset publicly available.
